title: Netra Job Status
$comment: C5 / INT-10c (decided 2026-09-20: upload and processing status are read by POLLING an HTTP job-status route). DRAFT by M2 (Ashlin); reviews: Arshad (M1 mounts the routes), Arun (M5 builds the screens). Routes, all requiring `Authorization: Bearer` and scoped by the caller's bound session like the existing /v1/sessions routes: (1) POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/uploads — multipart/form-data with fields `request_id` (UUID, one per logical upload; a retransmission replays), `title` (1-200 chars, shown to the student) and `file` (the document); responds 202 with {"job": Job}. The same request_id with the same bytes and title returns the same job (200); with different content it is 409 REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT. An unsupported or unreadable file is 422 INVALID_REQUEST with details.field = "file"; uploads are 503 RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE until the server has an approved maximum upload size configured (no default is invented). (2) GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/jobs/{job_id} — 200 with {"job": Job}. A job of another account, or an unknown job_id, is 403 AUTHORIZATION_DENIED for both, so the route is never an existence oracle. (3) GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/jobs — 200 with {"jobs": [Job, ...]}, the caller's most recent jobs, newest first, at most 20, so a restarted client can find work in progress. Errors use protocol/v1/error.schema.json as {"error": Error}. A job is READY only when its source can be opened and appears in GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/sources; the client then pins it with POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/source as usual. Polling: wait at least `poll_after_ms` between requests while the state is processing; stop polling on ready or failed.

job_id.$comment: Opaque, stable identity of one upload's processing. Not a source id and not a provider id.

kind.$comment: What is being processed. document_ingestion: an uploaded PDF (text layer, OCR fallback, reading blocks, search index). New kinds (for example uploaded or YouTube lecture video) are additive enum values in a later reviewed revision.

state.$comment: The three states the client presents: Processing, Ready, Failed. A job moves processing -> ready or processing -> failed and never back. `ready` means the source is openable; `failed` is terminal for this upload (the student may upload again).

stage.$comment: Optional finer progress while state is processing, for an accessible status line (for example 'Reading the document'). Absent when ready or failed. Stages are informational only; the client must not infer readiness from them.

title.$comment: The title the student gave the upload, echoed back. Untrusted text: display only.

source_id.$comment: The source this upload creates. Present once known; the same id appears in the sources list when ready.

source_version_id.$comment: The immutable version this upload creates; pin it with POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/source once state is ready.

failure.$comment: Present if and only if state is failed.

poll_after_ms.$comment: Server's suggested minimum wait before the next status request while processing. Absent when ready or failed.

reason.$comment: Closed vocabulary; never exception or provider text. unreadable_document: no readable text even after OCR, or a malformed PDF. unsupported_document: not a supported document type. content_mismatch: the stored bytes no longer match what was uploaded (integrity check). processing_failed: the service could not finish (retries exhausted); the document itself may be fine.

message.$comment: Safe, accessible wording chosen by the server for the reason. Never exception text, file paths or identifiers.

retryable.$comment: Whether uploading the same file again (with a NEW request_id) could succeed. False for unreadable/unsupported documents.

UploadForm.$comment: The multipart/form-data fields of POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/uploads, described as JSON for review. `file` is the binary part; its declared type must be application/pdf and its bytes must start with %PDF-.
